headline: Patrick Stewart has died at 84, actor's family confirms
summary: The acclaimed actor, known for his roles as Captain Picard and Professor X, passed away peacefully at his home.
details: Acclaimed actor Patrick Stewart, celebrated for his iconic roles as Captain Jean-Luc Picard in Star Trek: The Next Generation and Professor Charles Xavier in the X-Men film series, has passed away at the age of 84.
His family confirmed the news, stating that Stewart died peacefully at his home surrounded by loved ones. The cause of death was not immediately disclosed.

Stewart's career spanned over six decades, earning him numerous accolades, including multiple Emmy and Golden Globe nominations. He was also a distinguished stage actor, a member of the Royal Shakespeare Company, and a recipient of a knighthood from Queen Elizabeth II for his services to drama.

Tributes have poured in from across the entertainment industry, with colleagues and fans mourning the loss of a versatile performer and a beloved public figure. His legacy will undoubtedly continue to inspire future generations of actors and storytellers.

topic: reddit moves to logged-in only experience amid ai scraping concerns
headline_marked: Reddit [[moving to logged-in-only experience]] to protect data and boost engagement
headline: Reddit moving to logged-in-only experience to protect data and boost engagement
summary: The platform is testing a mandatory login requirement in select non-US markets this quarter, aiming to improve user retention and ad targeting.
details: Reddit is set to become a logged-in-only platform, a significant shift confirmed by CEO Steve Huffman. This move aims to enhance user experience by ensuring relevance and engagement, while also providing Reddit with more data for ad targeting.

The company cited the need to protect its valuable data corpus and adapt to evolving global regulations as key drivers for the change. Huffman stated that logged-in users are the most valuable, and they will be the primary focus going forward.

This transition comes as Reddit experienced a 'meaningful' drop in search referral traffic in Q3, with logged-out and web traffic seeing the largest impact. Current trends suggest a potential low-double-digit percentage fall in daily active unique users (DAUqs) for Q4 if the decline continues.

Reddit will begin testing the logged-in requirement in select non-US markets during Q4. The insights gained from these tests will inform the global rollout strategy, as Reddit aims to become a 'direct daily habit for every Internet user.'

The company has been implementing several changes to increase user engagement and data collection, including testing app requirements for mobile web users and restricting access to Old.Reddit.com for inactive accounts. The API pricing changes also effectively limited third-party app usage.
